content.title: About
content.content: Sprouted wheat toasted bread is a whole‑grain loaf made from germinated wheat kernels and lightly toasted to a golden crust. Germination preserves more vitamins, minerals and enzymes, while toasting adds a nutty aroma and a crisp crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sprouted grains contain up to 50 % more B‑vitamins and vitamin C than non‑sprouted grains.
Toasting enhances flavor and creates a denser crumb while retaining most nutrients.
This bread is popular in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines, where sprouted cereals have been eaten for centuries.
Sprouted wheat is rich in antioxidants that help combat free radicals.
The combination of sprouting and toasting gives a unique texture that many people prefer over regular whole‑grain bread.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Sprouted wheat provides thiamine, riboflavin, niacin and folate, which support energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, satiety and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Good source of minerals
items.content: The bread supplies magnesium, iron, zinc and selenium, essential for muscle function, immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains active enzymes
items.content: Germination retains enzymes that may aid the absorption of nutrients.

items.title: Moderate glycemic index
items.content: Toasting slightly raises the GI, but sprouted wheat bread still raises blood glucose more slowly than white bread.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with wheat allergy or celiac disease should avoid this bread.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: The product contains gluten, making it unsuitable for gluten‑free diets.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Like most whole‑grain breads, it is relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advised for weight management.

items.title: Possible mycotoxins
items.content: Improper sprouting can lead to mold growth; purchase from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bread plain, toasted, or topped with avocado, cottage cheese, hummus, or used for sandwiches. Light toasting brings out its nutty flavor. It pairs well with soups, salads and vegetable stews.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the loaf in a paper bag or cloth sack at room temperature for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag and re‑toast or warm in the oven before serving.
